A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEMOIR with the same authors, research objective, and core framework. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MEMOIR experiments on ZsRE, SelfCheckGPT, and Temporal, together with scalability tests and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original MEMOIR results on the retained benchmarks and adds activation-centering experiments and RippleEdits evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes mask construction from last-token activations to activations averaged across all prompt tokens, then centered using a reference mean from 100 irrelevant prompts. These alter the procedure, while the residual-memory architecture, TopHash permutation, and conditional retrieval framework remain intact.

E1.justification: v2 adds RippleEdits' POPULAR dataset for multi-hop reasoning. This substantially extends task coverage to logical consequences of edited facts and preservation of unrelated relations, beyond the retained factual Q&A, hallucination correction, and Temporal evaluations. Longer ZsRE edit sequences change sample counts rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: Named baseline membership is unchanged in corresponding retained comparisons. RippleEdits evaluates existing baselines: ROME, MEMIT, GRACE, AlphaEdit, and WISE. MEMIT's missing score at 15,000 edits concerns a newly introduced setting, not removal from the matched 7,000-edit comparison.

E3.justification: Table 4 replaces the 5,000-edit block with 15,000 edits while retaining 7,000. Appendix A.4.3 changes routing thresholds from 0.6 to 0.4 for LLaMA-3, 0.6 to 0.46 for LLaMA-2, and 0.55 to 0.4 for Mistral. RippleEdits introduces filtered 10- and 100-edit subsets, logical-generalization and relation-specificity metrics, and evaluation after the complete sequence.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 and Table 11 test whether centering matters and whether its reference-set size affects performance, comparing no centering with 10, 100, and 1,000 irrelevant prompts. Existing conditional-activation, forgetting, active-index-count, and mask-selection analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4.4 retains the same averaging practice and run counts, including 1,000 single-edit ZsRE experiments and 60 ten-edit SelfCheckGPT runs using different samples. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty reporting for the main results.

E6.justification: Numerous retained results change: LLaMA-3's 1,000-edit Q&A average falls from 0.95 to 0.93; locality without conditional activation rises from 0.28 to 0.68; and LLaMA-2's 600-edit hallucination perplexity changes from 1.09 to 1.48. v2 removes the 5,000-edit results and adds 15,000-edit, centering, and RippleEdits results. These are revised results under changed method/settings, not controlled same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Equations 1–4, mask-overlap definition, and Temporal probability-threshold formula remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version provides additional theorems or proofs. The new pooling and centering steps are procedural changes rather than new formal theory.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the claimed editing horizon from 7,000 to 15,000 and adds multi-hop reasoning to the claimed state-of-the-art evaluation coverage. The central contribution remains a sparse residual memory balancing reliability, generalization, and locality.

C2.justification: v2 explains centering as suppressing consistently dominant features and interprets its ablation as showing robustness to reference-set size. Section 3.2 narrows the irrelevant-data argument to avoiding large-scale irrelevant samples. It also introduces strong multi-hop generalization interpretations, although Table 14 does not support superiority over every baseline on logical generalization. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4.3 newly specifies GPT-J's edited layer, 70 iterations, 4,096 active indices, and 0.45 routing threshold for an already evaluated model. v2 also documents the centering reference data and RippleEdits filtering. Hardware, existing training-time disclosures, and the promise to release code upon acceptance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 introduces an attribution to the RippleEdits benchmark in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.5, but its citation renders as [?] without a bibliographic entry. The related-work discussion and all 44 numbered bibliography entries otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections and expands the mask-construction explanation. Appendix B gains centering and RippleEdits subsections, renumbering existing material. The main section order and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds centering, RippleEdits-example, and RippleEdits-results tables; expands Table 8 with separate irrelevant-prompt rows and corrects its OOD label; and relocates existing tables. Plot displays change, including Figure 6's vertical scales, but the overall figure organization and document design remain similar.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens assessment of long-horizon retention and tests logical propagation beyond v1's evaluations. The centering ablation and newly specified GPT-J settings also improve scrutiny and reproducibility. These gains are limited by reporting defects: Section 4.2 claims better multi-hop generalization than all baselines, whereas Table 14 gives MEMOIR 0.20 versus AlphaEdit's 0.22 at 100 edits; RippleEdits citations remain unresolved, and Appendix B.1 retains a stale average. Overall, the added evidence and documentation provide a limited net improvement.
